title: The Word was made flesh (CCC 456–460)
hook: God became human to save us, show us love, and share his life

segments.voice: Yesterday, original sin: a wound handed down, not a crime committed. Your line was wounded, not ruined. Did you say it in your head before you said anything out loud? Today, the Church's answer to the wound. Day three hundred three.

Sunday Mass. The whole church is standing, saying the Creed together, the words everyone knows by heart and half the room says on autopilot. And then, in the middle, a strange thing happens. At one line, every head goes down. People bow. On Christmas and on the feast of the Annunciation, they do more: they drop to one knee, right there in the pew, in the middle of a sentence. Kids who don't know why do it because the grown-ups do. The line is about God doing something no one expected. Today, the Word made flesh.
screen: `THE CREED, ON AUTOPILOT.` → `EVERY HEAD GOES DOWN.` → `ONE KNEE, MID-SENTENCE.`

segments.voice: The line is this: and by the Holy Spirit was incarnate of the Virgin Mary, and became man. First, the word. Incarnate comes from the Latin caro, carnis: flesh. It's the same root as carnivore and chili con carne. Incarnation means, bluntly, God in meat and bone. John's Gospel says it in the Douay-Rheims: "And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us." The Word is the eternal Son, who was with God and was God. And he took flesh. Second, why. The Catechism gives four reasons, and they're worth counting on your fingers. One: to save us, by reconciling us with God. Two: so that we might know God's love, which John says was shown by God sending his Son. Three: to be our model of holiness, a life you can actually watch. Four: to make us, in the words of Second Peter, partakers of the divine nature. Third, that last one surprises people. Early Christian teachers like Athanasius put it in a sentence that still stops readers: God became human so that humans might share in God's own life. The Church calls it divinization, and it doesn't mean we stop being creatures. It means God's life can be given to us. Fourth, the name. Matthew's Gospel calls the child Emmanuel, and explains it: "which being interpreted is, God with us." Not God above us, looking down. God with skin. God who got hungry, tired, and cold. That's why heads bow in the Creed: it's the moment Catholics remember that the distance between God and us was crossed from God's side.
screen: `CARO: FLESH.` · `SAVE, SHOW LOVE, MODEL, SHARE.` · `THAT WE MIGHT SHARE GOD'S LIFE.` · `EMMANUEL: GOD WITH US.` · then, large: `AND THE WORD WAS MADE FLESH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: bow at the words. Settle, and breathe. If you know the Creed, say it slowly to yourself, and when you reach and was incarnate, bow your head, or, if you're able and it feels right, go down on one knee, the way the Church does at Christmas. If you don't know the Creed, just say the six words: and the Word was made flesh. Then stay there. Notice your own flesh: your hands, your breath, the weight of your body. That's what Catholics say God took on. The bell holds the time.
Incarnation. From the Latin for flesh: the Son of God taking a real human body and soul, to save us, show us love, and share his life. Today's word.
Your line: god with skin. Today, when you eat, or get tired, or feel the cold, remember the Church's claim that God has felt it too. Day three hundred three.

howItsDone: At Sunday Mass, Catholics bow during the Creed at the words about the Incarnation, and on Christmas and the Annunciation they genuflect at those words instead.

match.prompt: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.
pairs: God became human so we might share God's life

myth: the Catechism gives only one reason for the Incarnation
it gives four: to save us, to show God's love, to be our model, and to share God's life.
incarnate shares a root with carnivore
both come from the Latin caro, carnis: flesh.
sharing God's life means people stop being creatures
Catholics say God's life is given to us while we remain creatures.

fork.setup: it's Christmas morning Mass. the Creed reaches and by the Holy Spirit was incarnate of the Virgin Mary. what does the congregation do?
options: genuflect, going down on one knee.
fork.reveal: on Christmas and the Annunciation Catholics genuflect at these words; on other Sundays they bow.

original.note: Greek, John 1:14: the Word became flesh. sarx is the plain word for flesh.

trapdoor: what you thought: Jesus was a good man God chose.
what it means: the eternal Son of God took real flesh, to save, to show love, to model holiness, and to share God's life.
what a scholar hears: John's sarx, a blunt word; Athanasius on divinization; 2 Peter 1:4, partakers of the divine nature; the Creed's bow.
